A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SUMO research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V1 reports original GLUE fine-tuning, C4 pretraining, GSM8K evaluation, and appendix MAWPS experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds zero-shot benchmark comparisons, Muon comparisons, and a hyperparameter sensitivity study.

M1.justification: Section 3.2, Algorithm 1, and Definition C.1 add the gradient component outside the selected subspace. The update direction changes from QO to G − Q(QᵀG − O), combining the gradient residual with the orthogonalized subspace update. This substantively changes the optimization procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds a ten-task zero-shot evaluation covering BoolQ, RTE, HellaSwag, Winogrande, OpenBookQA, ARC-Easy/Challenge, PIQA, SciQ, and MathQA. This substantially extends reasoning coverage; RTE also gains a zero-shot scenario beyond its retained GLUE fine-tuning evaluation.

E2.justification: New Table 6 evaluates SUMO against APOLLO and APOLLO-Mini alongside AdamW. Appendix Table 8 adds full-model Muon comparisons on five GLUE tasks. These introduce important evaluated comparators absent from the corresponding v1 comparisons; the original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: The added evaluations introduce LLaMA-350M pretraining with sequence length 1024 and a LLaMA-130M grid over ranks 128/256/512 and update frequencies 100/250/500/1000. Existing GLUE settings remain unchanged. The revised statement that C4 experiments reach 1B parameters matches a model size already present in v1 Table 3.

E4.justification: New Appendix Table 9 tests sensitivity to projection rank and subspace update frequency on LLaMA-130M/C4, comparing GaLore and SUMO across twelve configurations. The existing SVD-versus-Newton-Schulz analyses remain; no ablation isolates the newly added gradient residual.

E5.justification: V2 Table 8 first reports means and standard deviations for SUMO variants on five GLUE tasks, whereas v1 provides point estimates. This reporting is limited to selected results, and neither run counts nor seeds are specified; an increase in repeated runs is not established.

E6.justification: New Tables 6, 8, and 9 add zero-shot, Muon, and sensitivity results. The sweep includes GaLore outperforming SUMO at update frequency 1000 with ranks 256 and 512. Table 3 revises SUMO's reported 1B memory from 1.16G to 3.84G while retaining perplexity 14.68. Most original scores, including MAWPS results renumbered from Table 6 to Table 7, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.3 and Remarks 3.4/3.6 change selected dimension factors from m to n, including the admissible approximation-error threshold. The SVD operation-count expression and Definition C.1 also change. Appendix proofs are substantially retained; removed duplicate theorem statements are not removed theoretical results, and no new proof accounts explicitly for the gradient residual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the central claims: exact moment orthogonalization in adaptive low-rank subspaces improves convergence, stability, performance, and memory efficiency, including the claim of up to 20% memory savings.

C2.justification: V2 adds a mechanism explanation asserting that the gradient residual preserves stability without interfering with the orthogonalized moment and incurs negligible overhead. It also interprets the new zero-shot results as consistent downstream outperformance, although Table 6 contains OpenBookQA and SciQ exceptions. No corresponding qualification is added.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly explains how to implement the residual update by reusing the full gradient and projected gradient, avoiding explicit construction of the perpendicular component. Existing hardware disclosures, GLUE hyperparameters, and post-hoc adapter instructions remain; no new code or data access information is supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds benchmark references 56–64 to support the expanded zero-shot evaluation. The optimizer-related literature and central positioning against low-rank and approximate orthogonalization methods remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 copyedits existing prose, adds descriptive method-block headings, places Algorithm 1 after the block explanations, and repairs unresolved lemma references. It removes duplicated appendix theorem statements and adds a benchmark-details subsection while retaining the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds substantial new displays for the zero-shot benchmark comparison, Muon comparison with uncertainty, and hyperparameter grid in Tables 6, 8, and 9. It also relocates Algorithm 1 and Table 3, reduces Figure 2's displayed size, and expands shared hyperparameter entries into per-task cells. The plotted content of both figures remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens empirical documentation through direct Muon/APOLLO comparisons, sensitivity results, and partial uncertainty reporting. However, Algorithm 1 now includes the gradient residual while Appendix A's convergence argument still uses the earlier orthogonalized update and its norm bound. These benefits coexist with an unresolved mismatch between the revised method and a central theoretical guarantee, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
